name: Georgia
summary: Statutes: the only government-provided O.C.G.A. is the LexisNexis-hosted free annotated code, a JavaScript app that returns no text to either tool; Justia's 2025 Code of Georgia (tier 2, WebFetch only, shell blocked by Cloudflare) is the practical text source, with chapter indexes that show section ranges. Constitution: SOS 'Revised January 2023' PDF (WebFetch ok, truncates in Art. III; shell blocked). Court rules: Court of Appeals rules are per-group HTML pages on gaappeals.gov (script ok); Supreme Court Rules and the current Uniform Superior Court Rules are PDFs under gasupreme.us/wp-content/uploads/, which robots.txt disallows; an older USCR edition (through March 6, 2025) is readable on assets.georgiacourts.gov. Admin code: rules.sos.ga.gov subject pages are constructible and script-readable (per-rule URLs are robots-disallowed), Cornell LII mirrors per rule. Case law: Court of Appeals has a GET date search and GET docket record with efast PDFs (opinions with PDFs from ~2013); Supreme Court publishes yearly opinion lists (2017-) but the PDFs are robots-disallowed, so Justia is the readable route. Cert dispositions: Supreme Court granted/denied lists (2022-) show the Court of Appeals docket in parentheses, and the Court of Appeals docket record names the certiorari number.

citation_map.notes: Georgia's own court style omits periods in the regional reporter and puts it in parentheses after the official cite: 'Young v. Johnson, 359 Ga. App. 769, 770 (860 SE2d 82) (2021)', and writes subsections with spaces: 'OCGA § 9-11-12 (b) (6)'. There is no public-domain citation format. O.C.G.A. sections are always title-chapter-section (with optional decimals, e.g. 16-13-30.1); 'Code Section' in Georgia acts means O.C.G.A. A '§§ 9-11-12 to 9-11-16' or '§§ 9-11-12 - 9-11-16' range is two sections: the regex takes the first and refuses a following hyphen-digit. Bare 'Rule 33.2' or 'Rule 22' must not route here without 'Court of Appeals' / 'Supreme Court' / 'Georgia' context; 'Code Section' also needs Georgia context. 'Rule NNN-N-N-.NN' with the '-.' separator is distinctive of the Georgia administrative code. Georgia's Civil Practice Act (O.C.G.A. § 9-11-1 et seq.) and Evidence Code (Title 24) are statutes, not court rules, so 'Rule 12(b)(6)' arguments in Georgia cite O.C.G.A. § 9-11-12 (b) (6). Docket prefixes: Supreme Court S{yy}A appeal, S{yy}C certiorari petition, S{yy}G certiorari granted, S{yy}D discretionary application, S{yy}I interlocutory application, S{yy}Q certified question, S{yy}Y bar discipline, S{yy}Z judicial discipline; Court of Appeals A{yy}A appeal, A{yy}D discretionary, A{yy}I interlocutory, A{yy}E emergency (from listing observation and memory). Court of Appeals Rule 33.2: opinions decided before Aug. 1, 2020 with special concurrences or concurrences in judgment only are 'physical precedent only' and must be marked so when cited; unreported decisions (Rule 34) and Rule 36 affirmances have no precedential value. 'cert. denied' entries route here only with Georgia context. CourtListener ids ga / gactapp are from memory, unverified. Docket-number regex must be used only with Georgia context: S/A + 2-digit year + letter + 4 digits can collide with other courts' styles. 'Unif. Super. Ct. R.' without a 'Ga.' prefix routes here: no other state uses 'Uniform Superior Court Rules', but route only with Georgia context if another state's 'Unif. Super. Ct. R.' turns up.

access.pattern_rules: Title and chapter as plain integers from the citation (9-11-12 → title-9/chapter-11). Article (and part, where a chapter has parts) is NOT in the citation: read it from the chapter index, whose link texts show section ranges, e.g. 'Article 3 - Pleadings and Motions (§§ 9-11-7 — 9-11-16)'. Chapters without articles omit the segment (51-1-6 → /title-51/chapter-1/section-51-1-6/). Decimal sections: '.' becomes '-' (16-13-30.1 → section-16-13-30-1, verified at /title-16/chapter-13/article-2/part-1/section-16-13-30-1/). Year-specific: insert /{year}/ after /georgia/.
access.navigation: chapter index (article links with §§ ranges, em dash) → if an article link shows 'Pts.' instead of §§ (e.g. 'Article 2 - Regulation of Controlled Substances (Pts. 1 — 2)'), open the article page and choose the part by its §§ range (two index hops) → section page. Verified: 9-11-12 → /title-9/chapter-11/article-3/section-9-11-12/; 16-5-1 → /title-16/chapter-5/article-1/section-16-5-1/; 51-1-6 → /title-51/chapter-1/section-51-1-6/; 24-8-801 → /title-24/chapter-8/article-1/section-24-8-801/; 16-13-30.1 → /title-16/chapter-13/article-2/part-1/section-16-13-30-1/.

sources.coverage: Supreme Court 1850-2026; Court of Appeals 1910-2026. Latest Supreme Court item seen: Sept. 22, 2026 (Oct. 14 releases not yet posted).

access.pattern_rules: court-slug: supreme-court | court-of-appeals. year = decision year. docket_lower = first docket number lower-cased (S26A0604 → s26a0604; consolidated cases use the first). Duplicates may get a '-0' suffix (s26a0374-0.html) — check the year listing https://law.justia.com/cases/georgia/{court-slug}/{year}/ if the guess fails.

hazards: slip pagination, no Ga./S.E.2d star paging
Justia 'Date Decided' can be off by a day (A26A0857: Oct. 6 vs. Oct. 7, 2026 in the opinion header and court listing) — take the date from the opinion or the court listing

probe.expect: Appellant Sterling Ware challenges his 2024 convictions for malice murder

verification.evidence: WebFetch: full body 'Appellant Sterling Ware challenges his 2024 convictions for malice murder'; no reporter cite. Also /court-of-appeals/2026/a26a0896.html body 'After Mack Dekle was injured on a bike path'. | Independent check 2026-10-16: WebFetch: 'LAGRUA, Justice. Appellant Sterling Ware challenges his 2024 convictions for malice'; second citation Morrow GA Investors, LLC v. 1590 Adamson, LLC, A26A0857 (Ga. Ct. App. 2026) ok

sources.notes: The readable route for Supreme Court of Georgia text, since the Court's PDFs are robots-disallowed.

sources.title: Supreme Court of Georgia — certiorari petitions granted and denied (yearly lists)
sources.official_status_evidence: Court website listings.
sources.coverage: Granted and Denied pages for 2022-2026, by disposition date; each row gives the Supreme Court docket, case name and the Court of Appeals docket in parentheses. Also /2026-discretionary/ and /2026-interlocutory/ (applications granted).

access.pattern_rules: Search the page text for the Court of Appeals docket (e.g. 'A25A2138') — no party-name guessing needed. Try the decision year and the following year.

hazards: pre-2022 cert history must come from the Court of Appeals docket record

sources.title: Court of Appeals docket record — 'Supreme Court Information' block
sources.official_status_evidence: Docket system.
sources.coverage: Each Court of Appeals docket record lists any notice of intent, cert application date, certiorari number, disposition and remittitur; also 'Supreme Court Transfer'.
hazards: Disposition field lags: S26C1177 denied Oct. 14, 2026 still blank on Oct. 16

verification.evidence: fetch_doc.py grep: 'Notice of Intent March 25, 2026 Application Date April 6, 2026 Certiorari Number S26C1177'; Disposition blank. | Independent check 2026-10-16: script: 'Notice of Intent March 25, 2026 ... Certiorari Number S26C1177'; Disposition blank; second citation A24A1853 ok

sources.notes: Gives the cert number deterministically from the Court of Appeals docket; confirm the disposition on ga-cert-lists. On grant the record shows the G number with 'Disposition Granted' and date (A24A1853 → S25G0922, Aug. 12, 2025).

absent.what: public.law edition of the Georgia Code
absent.evidence: public.law lists only CA, CO, FL, NV, NY, OR, TX; georgia.public.law fails at the proxy (CONNECT 502).

absent.what: Cornell LII Georgia Code / Constitution / opinions
absent.evidence: law.cornell.edu/states/georgia links out to LexisNexis, sos.ga.gov, gasupreme.us, gaappeals.us; LII hosts only the Georgia regulations.

absent.what: Government-hosted O.C.G.A. text readable by tools, or official bulk download
absent.evidence: Only the LexisNexis free container (JS app, empty to both tools); legis.ga.gov is a JS shell. No bulk file found.
Georgia courts cite Ga./Ga. App. with parallel SE2d (e.g. '359 Ga. App. 769, 770 (860 SE2d 82) (2021)' in the Dekle slip opinion).

absent.what: Free official reporter (Ga., Ga. App.) pagination
absent.evidence: Court PDFs and Justia pages carry slip pagination only; Supreme Court says the bound Georgia Reports hold the official text.

script_candidates.why: Plain GET endpoints: date-range opinion list (docket, style, date, ruling, efast PDF uuid), docket record by case number, party search. Resolves (docket or date) → PDF deterministically and feeds subsequent history.

Constructible subject pages plus per-department PDF downloads (Download_pdf.aspx); a script can map rule → subject page and slice the rule by its 'Rule N-N-N-.NN' heading, avoiding WebFetch on 700K-char pages.
Yearly granted/denied HTML lists with Court of Appeals docket numbers in parentheses — a script can index COA docket → cert docket, date and disposition.

corpus_candidates.why: 145 pp, 351,798 chars; WebFetch stops in Rule 9.1 of 49. Edition is through March 6, 2025; the current 2026-04-09 edition is robots-disallowed on gasupreme.us.
53 pp, 118,679 chars — slightly beyond one WebFetch window; HTML group pages are an alternative.
WebFetch stops in Art. III § IX; but sos.ga.gov answers robots.txt with a bot check, so ingest.py cannot download it — not ingestable unless that changes.
Subject pages up to ~710K chars; WebFetch cannot reach later rules.
